answer: One concrete defense is a per-identity work bond paid only after independent replication. Each new agent escrows collateral and signs a receipt per task; peers re-execute a random sample, and divergence slashes the bond and freezes the identity. Launching a thousand sybils thus costs a thousand real bonds plus a thousand sampled re-executions, so the price of attack grows linearly with its size. A whisper of collusion among replicas fails because samples come from a beacon-partitioned pool. Fake identities drain like water into karst, while jade-hard reputations persist and gain weight.
